Early Childhood Education — Practice Portfolio

A collection of learning experiences planned and implemented by Khushi Patel during early childhood education placements, based on children's observed interests and designed to support the EYLF outcomes.

🎨 A note on the images: All activities shown here were genuinely planned and implemented with children during my placements, based on individual observations of their interests and to support an inclusive learning environment. As my placement centres have a no-filming/no-photography policy to protect children's privacy, real photographs of the children or centre could not be used. The images shown are AI-generated reference recreations of each set-up, included only to illustrate how each experience was presented — they are not photographs from the actual centres.
Kindergarten 🔴

Colour Treasure Hunt

Children searched through wet sand to discover, identify and count coloured balls while working collaboratively with peers. The experience developed colour recognition, early numeracy, problem-solving and communication skills while encouraging curiosity, persistence and active participation.

Outcome 4 – Confident & involved learnersOutcome 5 – Effective communicators
Kindergarten 🦋

Butterfly Painting – Symmetry Art

Children created butterfly paintings by adding paint to one side, folding and pressing the paper to reveal symmetrical patterns. Through hands-on exploration, they investigated colour mixing, creativity and symmetry while making independent choices.

Outcome 4 – Confident & involved learnersOutcome 5 – Effective communicators
Kindergarten 🔤

Letter M Sand Tracing

Children explored the uppercase and lowercase letter M through a hands-on sand-tracing experience. Using cotton buds, glue and coloured sand, they practised forming the letter while developing letter recognition, pencil grip, fine motor skills and hand-eye coordination.

Outcome 4 – Confident & involved learnersOutcome 5 – Effective communicators
Kindergarten 🌏

Cultural Diversity Circle Time

Children explored different cultures through images of traditional clothing, foods, festivals and places of worship. They were encouraged to voluntarily share their family experiences, languages and traditions, promoting respect, inclusion and belonging.

Outcome 1 – Strong sense of identityOutcome 2 – Connected & contribute to their world
Toddler Room 🐑

Little Farmer – Harvesting Grass

Children explored fresh grass and soil by harvesting grass, feeding toy farm animals and watering the remaining plants. The hands-on experience encouraged sensory exploration, confidence with natural materials, fine motor development, inquiry and understanding of living things.

Outcome 3 – Strong sense of wellbeingOutcome 4 – Confident & involved learners
Toddler Room 🐠

Sea Animal Sensory Discovery Tub

Children explored an ocean-themed sensory tub, searching for hidden sea animals and identifying their features and habitats. Through water, cornflour and aquatic materials, the experience encouraged sensory exploration, fine motor development, curiosity, language and early science concepts.

Outcome 4 – Confident & involved learnersOutcome 5 – Effective communicators
